MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  MARCH 22, 2016

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order at 7:02 p.m. in the City Council Chambers, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by
MAYOR ZUCKERMAN.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL
City Council Members Present: Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

City Staff Present:  City Manager Doug Prichard
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  Planning Director David Wahba
  Community Services Direct Andy Clark
  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis

Others Present:  Jeff Romanelli, Park and Activities Commission
  Victor Yoo, Planning Commission

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

  NONE

5.  ROUTINE MATTERS

A.  ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 23, 2016

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE THE ADJOURNED CITY  COUNCIL  MINUTES  OF
  FEBRUARY 23, 2016 AS PRESENTED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS – FEBRUARY AND MARCH

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL

  TO APPROVE WARRANTS 56550 THROUGH 56587 IN AN AMOUNT OF
  $375,470.71; SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 020116 THROUGH 020216;
  56060 (VOID); 56150 (VOID); 56370 THROUGH 56375; 56420
  THROUGH 56443; 56478 THROUGH 56488 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $221,398.81 FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF $596,869.52 WITH
  PROPER AUDIT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR: The following routine matters will be acted upon by one
  vote to approve with the majority consent of the City Council. There will be no
  separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior
  to the roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL

  TO APPROVE ITEMS A-C.
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
MARCH 22, 2016
 A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  Reading in full of all ordinances and resolutions presented for consideration to the
  City Council will be waived and all such ordinances and resolutions will be read
  by title only.

  APPROVED.

B.  FEBRUARY 2016 SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

C.  FEBRUARY MONTHLY REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

7.  AUDIENCE ITEMS  NOT  ON  THE  AGENDA/WRITTEN  AND  ORAL
  COMMUNICATIONS

A.  Captain Dan Beringer introduced himself to the COUNCIL noting that he is
  looking forward to working with the City. He commented that he has a long
  history with the Lomita Sheriff’s Station and was glad to be back.

B.  CALIFORNIA WATER SERVICE PRESENTATION

  Carmelo Sorce, California Water Service, provided a presentation of the Palos
  Verdes Pipeline Project that has been in the works for many years. Following
  extensive discussion, during which COUNCIL identified many issues of concern, it
  was noted that staff will be continue to monitor this project.

C.  ARTIFICIAL TURF INSTALLED IN PUBLIC RIGHT-OF-WAY; APPLICANT:  MR.
  AND MRS. KEN LIEU; LOCATION: 5114 KINGSPINE ROAD

  Recommendation: That the City Council take public testimony from Mr. and Mrs.
  Lieu regarding the artificial turf installed in the public right-of-way in front of their
  home at 5114 Kingspine Road and take one or more of the recommended actions
  as outlined in the report.

  Planning Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per agenda material). He
  noted that Ordinance No. 701 went into effect on February 26, 2016 and that the
  Rollingwood Homeowners’ Association opposed the Applicant’s artificial turf in the
  public right-of-way.

  In response to MAYOR ZUCKERMAN, Planning Director Wahba recalled the
  discussion when the Ordinance was first introduced and that the COUNCIL
  provided specific direction not to allow artificial turf in the public right-of-way.

  Ken Lieu, Applicant, commented that there was a miscommunication between his
  wife and Planning Director Wahba. He then asked the COUNCIL to exempt him
  from the Ordinance.

  Judy Bayer, President, Rollingwood Homeowners’ Association, noted that there
  are 375 homes in their association and that, while Mr. and Mrs. Lieu are lovely
  neighbors and keep their home well maintained, they objected to the artificial turf
  and requested the COUNCIL deny the Applicant’s request.

  In response to City Manager Prichard, Planning Director Wahba noted that one
  resident in that neighborhood also installed artificial turf and was subsequently
  directed to remove it from the right-of-way at the same time Mr. Lieu was
  informed.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
MARCH 22, 2016
   City Attorney Davis noted that previously existing Municipal Code Section
  12.20.060, which is still in full force and effect, must be interpreted by the
  COUNCIL in this case.

  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF commended Planning Director Wahba for allowing the
  COUNCIL to address this issue noting that he came up with good options to assist
  the Applicant with this situation. She further noted that the Applicant went
  through a great deal of expense to install this turf and that she would like to see
  this improvement remain in place.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN noted that artificial turf is not in keeping with the
  character of the City because of the natural environment. He pointed out that
  Mrs. Bayer was troubled by allowing one resident to keep the turf while making
  another resident remove theirs.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN noted that Planning Director Wahba is a very experienced
  director and that the miscommunication mentioned was probably more of a
  misunderstanding on the part of the resident. He further noted that homeowners’
  associations are very important and that he did not want to disempower their role
  in the neighborhood.

  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF noted her opinion that a resident should not be
  penalized for installing artificial turf in response to the drought.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO DIRECT MR. LIEU TO REMOVE THE ARTIFICIAL TURF FROM THE
  PUBLIC RIGHT-OF-WAY IN FRONT OF HIS PROPERTY WITHIN A
  REASONABLE TIME LIMIT, I.E. 30 DAYS, FINDING IT TO BE IN
  CONFLICT WITH PREVIOUSLY EXISTING MUNICIPAL CODE SECTIONS
  12.20.060 AND 12.20.080 WHICH ARE STILL IN FULL FORCE AND
  EFFECT.

  AYES:  Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  NOES:  Huff

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS/MEETINGS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-07-16; APPLICANT: THE CHADMAR GROUP
  AND ROLLING HILLS COUNTRY CLUB; LOCATION 26311 AND 27000 PALOS
  VERDES DRIVE EAST; REQUEST TO AMEND CITY COUNCIL RESOLUTION
  NO. 2260 (CONDITION OF APPROVAL NO. 68); APPROVAL OF A NEW BRIDLE
  TRAIL AND LANDSCAPE EASEMENT; SEWER EASEMENT; AND TEMPORARY
  PARKING LOT LOCATED AT THE NORTHEAST CORNER OF PALOS VERDES
  DRIVE NORTH AND PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Open the public hearing; 2) Take
  public testimony; 3) Discuss the issues; 4) Close the public hearing; 5) Adopt
  Resolution No. 2369; and 6) Approve all License and Easement Agreements
  included in the staff report.

  Planning Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per agenda material). He
  noted that a few minor changes were made to certain documents after the agenda
  was posted and emailed to the COUNCIL.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN noted that the Dapplegray Lanes Property Owners’
  Association (DLPOA) drafted a letter to the COUNCIL listing their requests that
  included: 1) The Rolling Hills Country Club “not do anything that blocks the
  natural water flow from across the Dapplegray Trail onto the Golf Club;” 2)
  Request for a “drainage study;” 3) “Not to approve any plans for Lot 114 until the
  impacts are known;” and 4) Not to approve the “Chadmar Homes application
  until that issue is adequately negotiated.”

  Planning Director Wahba noted that historically water from June’s Trail would
  drain onto the Country Club parking lot and flow out to Palos Verdes Drive East.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
MARCH 22, 2016
   Planning Director Wahba noted that he will meet with Willdan Engineering on the
  trail soon.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN opened the Public Hearing.

  Chuck Lande, Chadmar Group, emphasized that they have done what the
  COUNCIL has asked and is reflected in the exhibits and contracts.

  Paul Schwartz, 13 Sorrel Lane, commented that June’s Trail goes into the
  Dapplegray and Sorrel Lanes and is the only access to horse keeping facilities for
  19 homes. He noted that the difficulty is the turn in the trail because a large
  service vehicle would not be able to navigate that effectively, and that additional
  width is necessary.

  Paul Funk, 2110 Palos Verdes Drive North, Palos Verdes Loop Peninsula Trail
  Project, noted that they are working to make the 26 mile trail a reality. He noted
  their concern that the trails need to be contiguous and commended the Planning
  Department for a viable plan to enlarge the radius on the back corner of June’s
  Trail and resolving those critical issues to make sure it stays open.

  Haylie Pomroy, 25 Sorrel Lane, commented that June’s Trail was named after the
  home she occupies and requested the COUNCIL find a solution to the drainage
  prior to any approvals.

  Linda Robertson, 27121 Palos Verdes Drive East, noted her concern about
  emergency access.

  Joe Gelman, 52 Dapplegray Lane, noted his understanding that his and other
  adjacent properties would be significantly affected by lack of access. He asked the
  COUNCIL to delay approval until this matter is resolved.

  Jerry Gliksman, 87 Dapplegray Lane, reiterated his concern for the June’s Trail
  drainage as the water would affect not only that trail but the access point.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN noted that everyone needs to understand the
  parameters of this project because there are also private property issues in trying
  to create access that benefits the community.

  City Attorney Davis noted that language in the easement is not clear as far as
  vehicle access rights and may need further amendment.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN noted that service-oriented use is necessary to
  those homes that do not have access from the street.

  City Manager Prichard asked Planning Director Wahba about the point where the
  trail makes a jog to the left, and if the Traffic Engineer has determined an effective
  radius for vehicles to make that turn. Planning Director Wahba noted that he
  expressed this concern as well and will discuss it further with the Traffic
  Engineer.

  Mr. Lande expressed his concern regarding the community’s desire to require an
  easement from him on a piece of property that had no previous easement. He
  stated that he should not have to bear this responsibility for resolving these
  concerns and requested COUNCIL approval.

  Planning Director Wahba noted that the chain link fencing adjacent to Dapplegray
  Trail was addressed in the staff report, and that the Country Club offered to
  improve the fence in order to accent aesthetics of the golf course.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN reiterated that collaboration must take place to
  meet the needs of everyone involved and wanted reassurance that a three-rail
  fence will be installed behind the Dapplegray Trail.

  Bruce Steckel, 3 Strawberry Lane, Country Club Project Committee, noted the
  Club’s intention to remove the chain-link fence and replace it with a three-rail
  fence. He further noted that the developer may choose to retain the chain-link
  fence going to the Lomita Water Tower for security reasons.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
MARCH 22, 2016
   Lea Robertson, Palos Verdes Drive East, noted that they received notification in
  the mail of this public hearing. She asked the COUNCIL not to make any
  decisions at this time in order to receive input from affected residents who will be
  impacted.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN noted that the DLPOA has been intimately involved
  and engaged in this process for months.

  Mrs. Robertson commented that technically they are in the Dapplegray area, but
  they do not receive any notifications.

  Dale Allen, 39 Buckskin Lane, commented that this project is very confusing. He
  noted that the width of the trail really could not be determined and asked the
  COUNCIL to appoint a subcommittee.

  Ms. Pomroy noted her belief that an analysis was not undertaken to count how
  many vehicles travel the trail.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL inquired as to what the rights are on a prescriptive
  easement. City Attorney Davis noted that perhaps it was assumed that this
  easement was prescriptive, but in any case, it is beyond the City’s scope.

  Planning Director Wahba noted that without an engineering study, answers could
  not be provided with any certainty. He further noted that he asked the developer
  to provide an easement that matches the fence line to solve the issue with the
  turn, but the developer did not agree.

  Mr. Lande commented that he has always kept his word and wanted to be fair.

  Planning Director Wahba explained what exists there and what will be in place so
  that the public can be aware of what is happening.

  Joel Gelman, 52 Dapplegray Lane, commented that he will be the most impacted,
  and asked how the reduced trail width would affect drainage.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN asked if an improved exhibit could be presented to
  clarify the issues.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ noted that she believed the plans submitted were
  very clear for all parties involved and noted that they are online for the public to
  review.

  Mr. Lande noted that delaying a decision on the June’s Trail issues for two weeks
  would be acceptable, but requested that the COUNCIL take action on the balance
  of the issues at hand.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN

  TO ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2369.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  City Manager Prichard read Resolution No. 2369 by title only.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE THE LICENSE AGREEMENT FOR THE TEMPORARY
  PARKING LOT FOR ROLLING HILLS COUNTRY CLUB AS AMENDED.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN

  TO APPROVE THE SEWER EASEMENT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
MARCH 22, 2016
   COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN

  TO CONTINUE THE PUBLIC HEARING TO THE NEXT COUNCIL MEETING
  AND DIRECT STAFF TO CONTINUE TO WORK WITH THE APPLICANT
  AND THE NEIGHBORHOOD TO RESOLVE OUTSTANDING ISSUES ON
  JUNE’S TRAIL.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  ***

  At 10:12 p.m., MAYOR ZUCKERMAN called for a brief recess.

  ***
  At 10:14 p.m., the COUNCIL reconvened with MAYOR ZUCKERMAN,
  COUNCILWOMAN  HUFF,  COUNCILWOMAN  MITCHELL, and
  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ present.
  ***

9.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  SPECIAL PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 29, 2016

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE SPECIAL PLANNING COMMISSION
  MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 29, 2016.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

B.  SPECIAL PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 22,
  2016

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE SPECIAL PARK  AND  ACTIVITIES
  COMMISSION MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 22, 2016.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

C.  SPECIAL PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM FROM MEETING
  OF FEBRUARY 22, 2016 – RENAMING ARENA FOR DALE ALLEN

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the naming of the Dapplegray
  Park Round Pen as the "Dale Allen Round Pen Arena."

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL

  TO APPROVE THE NAMING OF THE DAPPLEGRAY PARK ROUND PEN
  AS THE “DALE ALLEN ROUND PEN ARENA.”

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

D.  MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING REGARDING ADMINISTRATION AND
  COST-SHARING FOR IMPLEMENTING THE COORDINATED INTEGRATED
  MONITORING PROGRAM FOR THE PENINSULA AGENCIES

  Recommendation:  That the City Council approve the Memorandum of
  Understanding between the Los Angeles County Flood Control District, the
  County of Los Angeles, and the Cities of Rolling Hills Estates, Rancho Palos
  Verdes, Palos Verdes Estates, Rolling Hills and to cooperatively fund and
  coordinate the payment and performance of monitoring and reporting services
  to implement the Coordinated Integrated Monitoring Program (CIMP) for the
  Peninsula Agencies and that the City Council authorize the Mayor to sign the
  MOU.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
MARCH 22, 2016
   Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material).

  Kathleen McGowan, Consultant, provided a presentation regarding the
  monitoring requirements for the Municipal Separate Storm Sewer System as
  well as the ongoing Total Daily Maximum Load (TMDL) conditions.

  *MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN returned at 10:21 p.m.

  In response to MAYOR ZUCKERMAN, Ms. McGowan noted that all five agencies
  have been involved in selecting the current contractor.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN noted that this is a good model for governance in
  having cities collaborate. He further noted that the City did administer this
  program for a period of time because it affected Machado Lake most directly.

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN, Ms. McGowan stated that
  provision of a 5% administrative fee which will be paid to City of Rancho Palos
  Verdes (who is now the lead agency) was not common practice at the time the
  City administered the contract.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN reiterated his concern with unfunded mandates.

  Ms. McGowan responded to various questions posed by the COUNCIL and
  provided a brief update on various findings of the monitoring process. She
  referred to a potential project at the Torrance Airport that could resolve much of
  the Peninsula’s water flow into Machado Lake and noted that the City of
  Torrance is researching grants to move this project forward.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO APPROVE THE MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING BETWEEN THE
  LOS ANGELES COUNTRY FLOOD CONTROL DISTRICT, THE COUNTY OF
  LOS ANGELES, AND THE CITIES OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES, RANCHO
  PALOS VERDES, PALOS VERDES ESTATES, ROLLING HILLS AND TO
  COOPERATIVELY FUND AND COORDINATE THE PAYMENT AND
  PERFORMANCE OF MONITORING AND REPORTING SERVICES TO
  IMPLEMENT THE COORDINATED INTEGRATED MONITORING PROGRAM
  (CIMP) FOR THE PENINSULA AGENCIES AND AUTHORIZE THE MAYOR
  TO SIGN THE MOU.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

10.  OLD BUSINESS

  NONE

11.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

12.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS: This item provides the
